held.title: Exit code 4 now means 'feature disabled' instead of 'recreate upgrade required'
held.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changes from 4 to 3, and 4 is reused for `FEATURE_DISABLED`. Anything that hardcodes the old value breaks quietly. That includes user scripts, and the operator's upgrade job logic, which this PR does not change. Such a caller would read the new 'feature disabled' failure (4) as 'recreate needed', and would see a real recreate result (3) as an unknown error. I could not see whether the operator uses this constant or a literal. Check every consumer of these exit codes. If the renumbering is intended, call it out as a breaking change, or give `FEATURE_DISABLED` a new code and leave 4 meaning recreate.
